answer: Reputation Decay Ledger. Each identity carries a history of completed work, and every new identity starts as a bare pearl with zero record, so any task requiring trust pays out only against accumulated history. An attacker cloning identities must fund each clone through the slow tide of real completed jobs before it earns anything, since fresh clones can't inherit the parent's record. The ledger also ties a relic of past transactions to each payout, meaning a clone farm pays full compute and labor cost per identity while the honest agent pays once and reuses its record.
